title: Continuity of sections at an inverse limit
statement:
Let $I$ be a directed set and $(X_j,f_{kj})_{j\in I}$ an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] over $I$ whose transition morphisms $f_{kj}:X_k\to X_j$ ($k\ge j$) are affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], every $X_j$ being quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; let $X=\varprojlim_jX_j$ with projections $f_j:X\to X_j$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Fix $i\in I$ and an abelian sheaf $F_i$ on $(X_i)_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and let $F_j=f_{ji}^{-1}F_i$ ($j\ge i$) and $F=f_i^{-1}F_i$ be its inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Let $j_0\ge i$ and let $W_{j_0}\to X_{j_0}$ be an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], an object of $(X_{j_0})_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]; put $W_k=W_{j_0}\times_{X_{j_0}}X_k$ ($k\ge j_0$) and $W=W_{j_0}\times_{X_{j_0}}X$ (fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]), objects of $(X_k)_{\Et}$ and $X_{\Et}$. For $k'\ge k\ge j_0$ let $\rho_{k'k}:F_k(W_k)\to F_{k'}(W_{k'})$ be the composite of the unit $\eta_{f_{k'k},F_k}$ of $f_{k'k}^{-1}\dashv f_{k'k,*}$ on sections over $W_k$, which lands in $(f_{k'k}^{-1}F_k)(W_k\times_{X_k}X_{k'})$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], of the composition isomorphism $c_{f_{ki},f_{k'k},F_i}:f_{k'k}^{-1}f_{ki}^{-1}F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}f_{k'i}^{-1}F_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], and of the restriction along the canonical isomorphism $W_{k'}\xrightarrow{\sim}W_k\times_{X_k}X_{k'}$ of iterated fibre products; let $\rho_k:F_k(W_k)\to F(W)$ be defined in the same way from the unit of $f_k^{-1}\dashv f_{k,*}$, the isomorphism $c_{f_{ki},f_k,F_i}:f_k^{-1}f_{ki}^{-1}F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}f_i^{-1}F_i$ and the canonical isomorphism $W\xrightarrow{\sim}W_k\times_{X_k}X$. Then $\rho_{kk}=\mathrm{id}$, $\rho_{k''k'}\circ\rho_{k'k}=\rho_{k''k}$, $\rho_{k'}\circ\rho_{k'k}=\rho_k$, and the induced homomorphism of abelian groups
$$
 \varinjlim_{k\ge j_0}F_k(W_k)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }F(W)
$$
is an isomorphism. In particular (take $j_0=i$, $W_i=X_i$ with the identity, and identify $W_k=X_i\times_{X_i}X_k\cong X_k$, $W\cong X$ canonically)
$$
 \varinjlim_{j\ge i}F_j(X_j)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }F(X).
$$

proof.text: *The system $(W_k)$ and its limit.* Write $s:W_{j_0}\to X_{j_0}$ for the given morphism, $p_k:W_k\to X_k$, $t_{kj_0}:W_k\to W_{j_0}$ ($k\ge j_0$) and $p:W\to X$, $t_{j_0}:W\to W_{j_0}$ for the projections. Base changes of etale morphisms are etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] (1), so $p_k$, $p$ are etale. Since $s$ is of finite presentation it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; these properties are stable under base change [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (3), so every $p_k$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and as $X_k$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated so is $W_k$ [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2). By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-over-limit] (with $T=W_{j_0}$, $S_j=X_j$, $0=j_0$), $(W_k,t_{k'k}=\mathrm{id}_{W_{j_0}}\times f_{k'k})_{k\ge j_0}$ is an inverse system over the directed set $I_{\ge j_0}$ with affine transition morphisms and limit $W$, with projections $t_k=\mathrm{id}_{W_{j_0}}\times f_k:W\to W_k$ (the $f_k$ being those of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]). From the definition of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]: $p_k\circ t_{k'k}=f_{k'k}\circ p_{k'}$ and $p_k\circ t_k=f_k\circ p$, and $\iota_{k'k}=(t_{k'k},p_{k'}):W_{k'}\to W_k\times_{X_k}X_{k'}$, $\iota_k=(t_k,p):W\to W_k\times_{X_k}X$ are the canonical isomorphisms of the statement; so these squares are cartesian. Put $w_k=f_{ki}\circ p_k:W_k\to X_i$ and $w=f_i\circ p:W\to X_i$; then $w_k\circ t_{k'k}=w_{k'}$ and $w_k\circ t_k=w$ (as $f_{ki}f_{k'k}=f_{k'i}$, $f_{ki}f_k=f_i$).

source.place: Theorem 09YQ (theorem-colimit), case p = 0, applied to the system (W_k)

proof.text: *A system of sheaves on $(W_k)$ with colimit $w^{-1}F_i$.* Put $H_k=w_k^{-1}F_i$ on $(W_k)_{\Et}$ and, for $k'\ge k\ge j_0$, $\varphi_{k'k}=c_{w_k,t_{k'k},F_i}:t_{k'k}^{-1}H_k\xrightarrow{\sim}(w_k t_{k'k})^{-1}F_i=H_{k'}$ [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2). Associativity of $c$ ([lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition] (1), with $(u,v,w)=(w_k,t_{k'k},t_{k''k'})$) is the cocycle condition $\varphi_{k''k}\circ c_{t_{k'k},t_{k''k'},H_k}=\varphi_{k''k'}\circ t_{k''k'}^{-1}\varphi_{k'k}$, and its unit law gives $\varphi_{kk}=e_{W_k,H_k}$; so $(H_k,\varphi_{k'k})$ is a system of abelian sheaves on $(W_k,t_{k'k})$ as in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-limit-of-schemes]. Its transition maps on $W$ are $\psi_{k'k}=t_{k'}^{-1}\varphi_{k'k}\circ c_{t_{k'k},t_{k'},H_k}^{-1}:t_k^{-1}H_k\to t_{k'}^{-1}H_{k'}$. Let $\gamma_k=c_{w_k,t_k,F_i}:t_k^{-1}H_k\xrightarrow{\sim}w^{-1}F_i$; associativity with $(u,v,w)=(w_k,t_{k'k},t_{k'})$ gives $\gamma_{k'}\circ\psi_{k'k}=\gamma_k$. Thus the $\gamma_k$ identify the system $(t_k^{-1}H_k,\psi)$ with the constant system of value $w^{-1}F_i$ and identity transitions; $I_{\ge j_0}$ is directed, hence connected, so the constant cocone is a colimit [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-constant-connected-diagram], and $(w^{-1}F_i,(\gamma_k)_k)$ is a colimit of $(t_k^{-1}H_k,\psi)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Theorem 09YQ (theorem-colimit), case p = 0, applied to the system (W_k)

proof.text: *Theorem 09YQ in degree $0$.* By step 1 the $W_k$ ($k\ge j_0$) are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, with affine transition morphisms and limit $W$; so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-limit-of-schemes] with $p=0$, applied to the system of step 2 and the colimit $(w^{-1}F_i,\gamma_k)$, shows that the maps $\theta_k=H^0(\gamma_k)\circ t_k^*$ induce a bijection $\varinjlim_{k\ge j_0}H^0((W_k)_{\Et},H_k)\to H^0(W_{\Et},w^{-1}F_i)$, the colimit taken along $H^0(\varphi_{k'k})\circ t_{k'k}^*$, which form a directed system by [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] (3),(4) and the cocycle condition of step 2. Translate to sections with [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-degree-zero]: the isomorphisms $\epsilon:\Gamma(T,-)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(T_{\Et},-)$ of its part (1) are natural in the sheaf, and by its part (2) $t^*\circ\epsilon=\epsilon\circ\eta_t(\text{global sections})$ ([def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]). Hence, with $\sigma_{k'k}=\varphi_{k'k}(W_{k'})\circ\eta_{t_{k'k},H_k}(W_k):H_k(W_k)\to H_{k'}(W_{k'})$ and $\sigma_k=\gamma_k(W)\circ\eta_{t_k,H_k}(W_k):H_k(W_k)\to(w^{-1}F_i)(W)$: $\sigma_{k''k'}\sigma_{k'k}=\sigma_{k''k}$, $\sigma_{k'}\sigma_{k'k}=\sigma_k$, and the induced map $\varinjlim_{k\ge j_0}H_k(W_k)\to(w^{-1}F_i)(W)$ is bijective.

source.place: Theorem 09YQ (theorem-colimit), case p = 0, applied to the system (W_k)

proof.text: *Comparison of the two systems.* Let $\rho^{\mathrm{res}}$ be the isomorphisms $q^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}G|_{V}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (1) for the etale $q=p_k,p$ (natural in $G$), and define the bijections $\alpha_k=c_{f_{ki},p_k,F_i}(W_k)\circ\rho^{\mathrm{res}}_{F_k}(W_k)^{-1}:F_k(W_k)\to\Gamma(W_k,p_k^{-1}F_k)\to H_k(W_k)$ and $\alpha=c_{f_i,p,F_i}(W)\circ\rho^{\mathrm{res}}_{F}(W)^{-1}:F(W)\to(w^{-1}F_i)(W)$ ([lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]; $w_k=f_{ki}p_k$, $w=f_ip$). Claim: $\alpha_{k'}\circ\rho_{k'k}=\sigma_{k'k}\circ\alpha_k$ and $\alpha\circ\rho_k=\sigma_k\circ\alpha_k$. For the first, let $b\in F_k(W_k)$, $a=\rho^{\mathrm{res}}_{F_k}(W_k)^{-1}(b)$, $t=t_{k'k}$. [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-pullback-unit] for the cartesian square $(g,p,g',p')=(f_{k'k},p_k,t,p_{k'})$ of step 1 and the sheaf $F_k$ gives $(f_{k'k}^{-1}F_k)(\iota_{k'k})(\eta_{f_{k'k},F_k}(W_k)(b))=\rho^{\mathrm{res}}(W_{k'})(\kappa(W_{k'})(\eta_t(W_k)(a)))$ with $\kappa=c_{f_{k'k},p_{k'}}^{-1}\circ c_{p_k,t}$ at $F_k$. Apply $c_{f_{ki},f_{k'k},F_i}(W_{k'})$, which commutes with restriction along $\iota_{k'k}$ (a morphism of sheaves): the left side becomes $\rho_{k'k}(b)$ by definition; on the right, naturality of $\rho^{\mathrm{res}}$ moves it inside as $p_{k'}^{-1}(c_{f_{ki},f_{k'k}})$. So $\alpha_{k'}(\rho_{k'k}(b))=[c_{f_{k'i},p_{k'}}\circ p_{k'}^{-1}c_{f_{ki},f_{k'k}}\circ c_{f_{k'k},p_{k'}}^{-1}f_{ki}^{-1}\circ c_{p_k,t}f_{ki}^{-1}](W_{k'})(\eta_t(W_k)(a))$, which by associativity of $c$ ([lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition] (1), $(u,v,w)=(f_{ki},f_{k'k},p_{k'})$) is $[c_{f_{ki},f_{k'k}p_{k'}}\circ c_{p_k,t}f_{ki}^{-1}](W_{k'})(\eta_t(W_k)(a))$. On the other side, naturality of the unit $\eta_t$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] along $c_{f_{ki},p_k,F_i}$ gives $\sigma_{k'k}(\alpha_k(b))=[c_{w_k,t}\circ t^{-1}c_{f_{ki},p_k}](W_{k'})(\eta_t(W_k)(a))$, and associativity with $(u,v,w)=(f_{ki},p_k,t)$ turns it into $[c_{f_{ki},p_kt}\circ c_{p_k,t}f_{ki}^{-1}](W_{k'})(\eta_t(W_k)(a))$. Since $p_kt=f_{k'k}p_{k'}$ (step 1) the two agree. The second identity is the same computation for the cartesian square $(f_k,p_k,t_k,p)$, with $\iota_k$, $f_{ki}f_k=f_i$ and $p_kt_k=f_kp$.

source.place: Theorem 09YQ (theorem-colimit), case p = 0, applied to the system (W_k)

proof.text: *The system identities.* By step 4, $\rho_{k'k}=\alpha_{k'}^{-1}\sigma_{k'k}\alpha_k$ and $\rho_k=\alpha^{-1}\sigma_k\alpha_k$. Hence $\rho_{k''k'}\rho_{k'k}=\alpha_{k''}^{-1}\sigma_{k''k'}\sigma_{k'k}\alpha_k=\alpha_{k''}^{-1}\sigma_{k''k}\alpha_k=\rho_{k''k}$ and $\rho_{k'}\rho_{k'k}=\alpha^{-1}\sigma_{k'}\sigma_{k'k}\alpha_k=\rho_k$ by step 3. For $\rho_{kk}=\mathrm{id}$: $\sigma_{kk}=e_{W_k,H_k}(W_k)\circ\eta_{\mathrm{id},H_k}(W_k)$ (step 2), read through $W_k\cong W_k\times_{W_k}W_k$, is the identity by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (3), so $\rho_{kk}=\alpha_k^{-1}\alpha_k=\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Theorem 09YQ (theorem-colimit), case p = 0, applied to the system (W_k)

proof.text: *Conclusion for $W$.* By step 5 the abelian groups $F_k(W_k)$ with the homomorphisms $\rho_{k'k}$ (all maps involved are maps of abelian sheaves on sections, hence additive) form a directed system with compatible family $(\rho_k)$, inducing a homomorphism $\rho:\varinjlim_{k\ge j_0}F_k(W_k)\to F(W)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] (ring $\mathbf Z$) the map induced by a compatible family $(\tau_k)$ out of a directed system $(M_k,\mu_{k'k})$ of abelian groups is bijective iff (a) every element of the target is some $\tau_k(x)$ and (b) $\tau_k(x)=\tau_k(y)$ implies $\mu_{k'k}(x)=\mu_{k'k}(y)$ for some $k'\ge k$ (use its parts (1), (2) and a common upper bound). Step 3 gives (a), (b) for $(H_k(W_k),\sigma_{k'k},\sigma_k)$, and the bijections $\alpha_k$, $\alpha$ carry them to $(F_k(W_k),\rho_{k'k},\rho_k)$ by step 4. So $\rho$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Theorem 09YQ (theorem-colimit), case p = 0, applied to the system (W_k)

proof.text: *The case $W=X$.* Take $j_0=i$ and $W_i=X_i$ with $\mathrm{id}_{X_i}$, which is etale (an isomorphism is locally of finite presentation, flat and unramified [def-weil-etale-morphism]) and of finite presentation (quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]). The projections $W_k=X_i\times_{X_i}X_k\to X_k$ and $W\to X$ are isomorphisms; restriction along them is an isomorphism $F_k(W_k)\cong F_k(X_k)$, $F(W)\cong F(X)$, and transporting the system $\rho_{k'k}$, $\rho_k$ along these isomorphisms gives the system of the unit maps on global sections followed by $c$. Hence $\varinjlim_{j\ge i}F_j(X_j)\cong F(X)$ by step 6.
